hints: Remember what the orange colour of bromine water disappearing actually tests for in organic chemistry.
Look carefully through A to D for a C=C double bond, the group that undergoes rapid electrophilic addition with bromine at room temperature.
Check which formula contains an alkene linkage hidden between carbons, then link that addition reaction to the loss of the orange colour.
walkthrough:
**Recall the bromine water test**

Think of $\text{Br}_2(\text{aq})$ as your detector for unsaturation. Orange bromine water is decolourised when $\text{Br}_2$ adds across a C=C double bond.

$$\text{C=C + Br}_2 \rightarrow \text{C(Br)-C(Br)}$$

**Identify the functional group in each compound**

Read each condensed formula for its reactive group. A is a carboxylic acid, $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$, B is an aldehyde, $\text{-CHO}$, and D is an ester, $\text{-CO}_2\text{-}$. None of these react with $\text{Br}_2(\text{aq})$ in this way.

Only C, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, contains a C=C alkene bond plus an alcohol $\text{-OH}$ group.

**Conclude which decolourises bromine**

The alkene in C undergoes electrophilic addition, using up the orange $\text{Br}_2$ to form a colourless dibromo product. So that is the compound that gives a positive test.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ is hexanoic acid, a saturated carboxylic acid. The $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ group does not react with bromine water, so the orange colour remains.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ is hexanal, a saturated aldehyde. Although aldehydes are reducing agents, they do not decolourise $\text{Br}_2(\text{aq})$ by addition, a common confusion with Tollens or Fehling tests.
options.C: Correct. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ is an unsaturated alcohol containing a C=C double bond. Bromine adds rapidly across the double bond to give a colourless dibromo compound, so orange $\text{Br}_2(\text{aq})$ is decolourised.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ is ethyl butanoate, a saturated ester. Esters are unreactive toward bromine water under these conditions, so no decolourisation occurs.
